claims.text: As-prepared HfNbTiVAl10 has a well-defined hierarchical heterostructure containing nanoscale precipitates and lamellar or multiscale interfaces.
The stated hierarchical heterostructure can be produced in HfNbTiVAl10 by standard casting and heat-treatment processes.
SEM and TEM measurements can provide quantitative phase-fraction, interface-density, precipitate-spacing, and hierarchical-length-scale descriptors for the proposed model.
A machine-learning or reduced-order framework using those descriptors will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture behavior in HfNbTiVAl10.
The descriptor-based model will produce predictions within minutes rather than hours.
The model will predict Young's modulus with less than 5% error.
The model will predict yield strength with less than 10% error.
The distribution of nanoscale precipitates and interphase boundaries governs load transfer in the alloy.
The distribution of nanoscale precipitates and interphase boundaries governs dislocation mobility in the alloy.
Interphase-boundary characteristics govern crack propagation and fracture behavior in HfNbTiVAl10.
Solid-solution strengthening is one of the mechanisms affecting the modeled mechanical response.
Precipitation strengthening and interface-induced toughening affect yielding and fracture in HfNbTiVAl10.
Using microstructural descriptors allows the model to capture the relevant physical mechanisms statistically.
The descriptor-based model bypasses the computational expense of full-scale simulations while retaining the effects of underlying physical interactions.
Prediction errors will be reduced by approximately 30–50% relative to established simulation methods.
Established full-scale finite-element or atomistic approaches typically require hours of computation.
Established simulations typically predict yield strength and elastic modulus with error margins exceeding 10%.
Prediction performance may deteriorate when unmeasured defects, extreme heterogeneity, out-of-range temperatures, or out-of-range loading conditions are encountered.
The achievable accuracy and efficiency depend on microstructural-data quality, imaging resolution, model training, and processing-batch variation.
